when: before 2:00
asks: where did their jungler start
which side is he starting
how do I tell where their jungler is
where's their jungler at
did he start top or bot
say: Watch which of their lanes shows up late; he likely started beside it. Path away for safe farm, or end near him to fight the crab.
more: A lane that helped with the first camp reaches its wave a moment late or missing a little health. That is the best free clue you get all game.
A full clear ends on the opposite side from where it started, so knowing his start tells you which river he reaches around when the crabs spawn at 2:55.
Pathing away from him gives both junglers quiet farm. Pathing to meet him sets up an early fight, which only pays if your lanes on that side can walk over first.
check: Which enemy lane reached its wave late or already missing health? I can't see lane arrivals.
breaks: Some junglers start alone and nobody arrives late. Then you have no read; ward the river you are clearing toward and treat both sides as live.
basis: written

when: before 3:00
asks: he started bot side where does he end up
their bot came late so where's he going
he's pathing up right
where will he be after his clear
say: If their bot lane came late, he likely started bot and ends top side. Finish bot to dodge him, or finish top with your laner ready.
more: A full clear runs through all six camps and comes out at the far river around level 4, near the time both crabs spawn at 2:55.
Ending opposite him gives you a free crab and a gank on the lane he just left. Ending beside him means a two on two with whichever lanes can move.
Tell your top laner now. A lane that knows he is coming in a minute keeps the wave back and makes his whole path worth nothing.
check: Did their bot lane really arrive late or hurt? I can't see lane arrivals. And is your top lane pushed in or able to move to river?
breaks: If he shows in a kill or assist before 3:00 he cut the clear short and this read is dead. Go by where he showed instead.
basis: rule

when: before 3:00
asks: he started top side where's he ending
their top came late so where's he headed
is he coming bot
where does he finish
say: If their top lane came late, he likely started top and ends bot side. Warn bot and finish there to fight, or take the top crab.
more: Junglers often path toward bot early because a two-player lane pays more for a gank and the first dragon is on that side.
If you finish bot too, the fight is decided by which bot lane has the wave. If you finish top, you get the crab and a free look at their top laner.
Either way your bot lane should hear it. A ping one minute early is worth more than arriving ten seconds late.
check: Did their top lane really arrive late or hurt? I can't see lane arrivals. And does your bot lane have the wave or are they stuck under tower?
breaks: If your bot lane is losing hard, meeting him there loses the two on two as well. Take the top side crab and gank top instead.
basis: rule

when: before 2:55
asks: is their jungler coming
can I fight right now or is he near
am I safe to push early
where's their jungler
should I be scared of a gank yet
say: Most junglers are still clearing until the crabs at 2:55, so trade now if you win it, or hold the wave if he ganks early.
more: A full clear takes a jungler to about level 4 and puts him at river around when the crabs spawn at 2:55. Before that, a gank usually means he gave up camps to do it.
That is your freest window in lane. Use it to win the push or the health bars, because after the crabs the map gets dangerous.
The exception is a jungler built to gank after two or three camps. Against one of those, play as if he is already in the brush.
check: Who is their jungler, and did you see the lane next to you arrive late? I can't see where he is.
breaks: If the lane next to yours leashed for him, a short clear puts him beside you early. Keep the wave on your half until he shows somewhere.
basis: pro:A lane that fights early without a ward invites a short clear

when: game time between 2:55 and 4:00 and their jungler has not appeared in any kill event
asks: where's their jungler now
is it gank time
can I keep pushing
should I back off
he hasn't shown where is he
say: First clears are ending, so he's likely at a crab or heading to a lane. Drop the wave back, or ward river and keep pushing.
more: Both crabs spawn at 2:55 and a full clear finishes around level 4. This is the first minute where every jungler has a reason to be in river.
A ward at this moment covers the most dangerous gank of the early game. Without one, a wave on your side of the lane is what keeps you alive.
If he shows on the far side, you get the push back for free and can crash the wave before recalling.
check: Is your river warded, and which side did he start? I can't see wards or where he is.
breaks: If he just appeared in a kill on the far side of the map, ignore this and push while you have the minute.
basis: rule

when: their jungler has a kill or assist before 3:00
asks: he ganked already what does that mean
their jungler ganked super early
he skipped camps right
what did he give up for that gank
say: He probably skipped camps for that, so he's behind on farm. Full clear and out-level him, or take camps on his far side now.
more: A gank that early usually means he walked past camps to make it. A full clear gets you to about level 4; he is behind that pace unless the kill paid for it.
Taking his far-side camps widens the gap, but only go if your lane there can follow. Finishing your own clear is safer and can still leave you a level up at the first crab.
Whichever you pick, he probably heads back to those skipped camps next, which makes him easier to find for a minute.
check: Which lane did he gank, what level is he, and are your lanes on his far side able to follow you in?
breaks: If the gank got him a kill and your lane there is now dead or recalled, do not walk in alone. Take your own camps and the crab on the other side.
basis: pro:An early gank is paid for in camps

when: their jungler's CS is well below yours and he has no kills, assists or deaths
asks: his cs is really low where is he
their jungler has no farm what's he doing
why is he so far behind in cs
he's not farming so where is he
say: Low farm with no kills usually means he's been waiting on a lane. Ping the lane you suspect, or out-farm him on the other side.
more: Farm that is missing with nothing to show for it was probably spent waiting in a brush. He tends to go back to the lane he has already invested in.
You can punish it two ways: show up behind him for the counter gank, or stay away and take camps and a crab while he waits.
Out-farming is the quieter win. Two or three clears of this and you are a level and an item ahead at the next objective.
check: Which of your lanes is pushed up or has no Flash? That's where he's most likely waiting.
breaks: If you've been taking his camps, or he just recalled, low CS only means he's behind, not hiding. Once his CS starts climbing again, drop the warning.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

when: their jungler's CS is above yours and he has no kills or assists
asks: he's just farming right
their jungler never ganks
he's out-farming me what do I do
is he a farm jungler
do I just farm with him
say: He's been farming, not ganking, so far. Match his clears and gank when your camps are down, or take his far side when he shows.
more: High farm and no kill involvement means his time has gone into camps. Your lanes have had it easier than usual, but that can change on his very next clear.
Small camps come back about 2:15 after they die, so he is on a clock. He shows up at lanes mostly in the gaps between clears.
If you let him farm for free he arrives at the mid game stronger than you. Either keep pace or make your ganks count.
check: Is he a champion that wants to scale, or one that's just having a quiet game? I only see his numbers.
breaks: The moment he shows up in a kill event, that read is over. Tell your lanes to respect him again, and never call the map safe just because he farms.
basis: pro:Gank when your camps are down

when: their jungler is at least one level above you
asks: he's a level up on me where's he going
their jungler's ahead what's he gonna do
is he gonna invade me
how do I play when he's ahead
say: A jungler a level up often comes looking for you. Farm beside your winning lane, or ward your camps and trade for his far side.
more: A jungler who is ahead wants a duel, and the easiest place to get one is on your camps beside a lane of yours that is pushed in.
So treat the side next to your losing lane as his for now. Give it up and take his opposite side when he shows on yours.
A level gap closes with a couple of quiet clears. A death to an invade makes it two levels.
check: Which of your lanes is stuck under tower right now? The jungle beside it is the unsafe half.
breaks: If all three lanes have push you can stand your ground; he gets collapsed on. Fight him with help, not alone.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: you are at least one level above their jungler and ahead of him in CS
asks: he's behind where's he gonna go
their jungler's down a level where is he
how do I find him when he's behind
what's he doing now that he's behind
say: He's short on safe farm, so he's likely beside his winning lane. Meet him there with your laner, or take the other side unopposed.
more: A trailing jungler has few places to stand. He can't walk into river alone, so he farms what is safe and looks for one cheap gank.
That makes him predictable for you and for your lanes. Your weakest lane is the one he is most likely to try.
Don't get lazy with it. He knows where you want to go as well, and a behind jungler with two teammates is not behind in that fight.
check: Which of their lanes is winning? His safe camps are next to it.
breaks: If their lane on that side has push, they arrive before your help does. Take the far side and a crab or camp instead of forcing it.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler's item list just gained an item (not a used potion or ward)
asks: he just bought something where is he
their jungler just recalled right
he backed what now
he's got a new item where's he coming from
say: A new item means he's at his fountain right now. Use his walk back for a quick gank or objective, or recall and match his buy.
more: A new item is the one moment the scoreboard tells you exactly where he is: in base. He has to walk all the way out from there.
He also comes back stronger than he left. If your own gold is unspent, the next river fight is tilted his way.
So use the walk time, then decide whether you need your own recall before meeting him.
check: How much gold are you sitting on, is a lane ready, and is the objective actually up?
breaks: If you are low on health or holding a lot of gold, use his recall to take yours too and meet him even.
basis: pro:Their jungler or carry in base is your window

when: their jungler is level 6 and you are level 5
asks: he's six and I'm not
their jungler hit six first
he's got ult and I don't where do I go
do I fight him at five
say: He has his ultimate first, so skip the river fight. Finish camps to reach six, or gank the lane farthest from where he last showed.
more: Level 6 is the biggest single jump in the early game. A fight at five against six usually goes to the six even if you were winning before.
Warn your lanes too. His first ultimate will be spent on whichever of them is pushed up.
One or two camps or a crab closes the gap. Rushing that is better than donating a kill to prove a point.
check: How close are you to six? I can't see your XP bar, only your level.
breaks: If two of your laners are already six and nearby, the numbers beat his level. Then you can take the fight.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

when: you are level 6 and their jungler is level 5
asks: I'm six he's five
I hit six first what do I do with it
I've got ult and he doesn't
should I go find him
say: You have a short window before he matches you. Force him off a crab or camp now, or spend your ultimate on a gank.
more: Being first to six is a lead with an expiry. Every camp he finishes shortens it.
Fighting him directly sets his clears back for minutes. Ganking with it turns the level into gold for a laner, which lasts longer.
The losing play is to keep farming as if nothing changed.
check: Where did he last show, and is a crab alive on that side?
breaks: If you can't find him within one camp's time, stop looking and take the gank. Hunting an empty jungle wastes the window.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

asks: when will he be back at his camps
how do I time his clears
how do I know when his camps are up
where will he be in two minutes
say: Small camps return about 2:15 after dying. Note the clock when he shows on one side, then ward it or wait there when the timer's up.
more: Junglers follow their camps. If you know when a side was cleared, you know roughly when he has a reason to be back.
Buffs take five minutes, so a buff you saw die is a second appointment you can plan a ward or a steal around.
This is how you tell lanes where the danger is without seeing him: he is near whatever just respawned.
check: What time did you last see him, and on which side? I can't see camps, so you hold that number.
breaks: A jungler who is ganking instead of clearing ignores the timers. If he shows in kill events between clears, track his kills, not his camps.
basis: rule

when: their jungler is alive and has had no kill, assist or objective event for over a minute
asks: I have no idea where he is
we lost their jungler
nobody's seen him
where could he be
he's been missing forever
say: No sighting means assume he's near your most pushed-up lane. Ping that lane back, or put a ward on his camps to find him.
more: When nobody has seen him, the safe guess is that he is wherever it would hurt you most.
That is usually the lane with the wave at their tower, or the objective that is about to spawn.
One deep ward on a camp that is due to respawn turns the guess into a sighting for the next couple of minutes.
check: Has anyone on your team actually seen him? Which of your lanes is pushed farthest, and what objective is up next?
breaks: If an objective is spawning within a minute, he's there, not in a lane. Move to it with your team instead.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: their jungler got a kill or assist on your bot lane or took dragon in the last 30 seconds
asks: he's bot can I push
their jungler showed bot
am I safe top now
can I trade now that he's bot
say: He just showed bot, so you have a safe window. Push for plates, or crash the wave and recall for free.
more: Top is the farthest lane from where he just was. Even if he comes straight to you it takes him a while, and he usually clears on the way.
A crashed wave and a clean recall puts you an item ahead for the next trade. Plates are better if you already have the health to stay.
Windows like this are how a lane gets ahead without ever fighting the jungler.
check: Is the enemy mid still in lane? A roaming mid can stand in for the jungler.
breaks: If you're low or their top laner out-trades you, crash the wave and recall instead of staying for plates.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: their jungler got a kill or assist on your top laner or took grubs or herald in the last 30 seconds
asks: he's top are we safe
their jungler showed top side
can we push bot now
can we go for a trade now
is dragon free
say: He's top side, so bot is yours for a bit. Shove and take plates, or call your jungler down and start dragon.
more: Their jungler can't be in two halves of the map. The moment he commits top, a two on two is really a two on two.
Dragon is the bigger prize if it's alive and your jungler is close. Plates are the sure thing if he isn't.
Either way, push the wave first. It is what lets you leave lane without losing farm.
check: Is dragon alive, and where is your own jungler? Is their mid still in lane?
breaks: If their mid is missing or their bot lane out-damages you two on two, take the safe plates-and-recall and skip the all-in.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

asks: which side do I stand on
where's their jungler coming from
how do I not get ganked mid
which side should I ward
what side is he on
say: Ward one river and hug that side of the lane. With no ward, hug the side your jungler is on, or stay back.
more: Mid has two entrances and you can only watch one. Standing on the warded side turns a gank into a long walk you can see coming.
When their jungler shows on one side, you have a short window to push or roam before he can cross to you.
A mid who tracks him also frees both rivers for their own jungler. That is how early crabs and invades get won.
check: Which river did you ward, where is your own jungler, and where did theirs last show? I can't see wards or positions.
breaks: If both sides are dark and he hasn't shown in a while, play in the middle of your own half and give up the push until someone sees him.
basis: written

when: your jungler got a kill, assist or objective on the far side of the map in the last 30 seconds
asks: my jungler's on the other side am I okay
our jungler is far away
should I play safe while he's top
nobody can help me right
say: Your help is across the map, so their jungler's best answer is you. Give the wave and stay healthy, or ward deep and keep farming.
more: When one side of the map is taking something, the other side pays for it if it stays pushed up.
A few lost minions is the price of the play your team is making. A death here cancels it out.
Once your jungler shows back on your side, you can step up again.
check: Is their jungler accounted for in that fight? If he showed there too, you're fine.
breaks: If their jungler was in that far-side fight, the opposite is true: push hard, you have the freest minute of the lane.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: their jungler's dead can I push
he's dead what do I do
is it safe now
their jungler just died
say: Their jungler is dead, so no jungle gank is coming until he's back. Push for plates or tower, or help your jungler take an objective.
more: A respawn timer is the one time you know exactly where he is. Use all of it.
He respawns at base and has to walk out, so the lanes farthest from his fountain get a little extra time.
If an objective is up, that usually beats plates. Without their Smite it is much easier to finish.
check: How long is left on his timer, and is their mid or support missing?
breaks: A roaming mid or support can still collapse on you. If one is missing, take the wave and stop short of their tower.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: their jungler has two or more kills or assists on the same one of your lanes
asks: he keeps ganking top
he's camping my bot lane
their jungler lives in that lane
he ganked the same lane again
say: He's camping that lane, so you know where he is. Sit behind it for the counter gank, or take everything on the opposite side.
more: Junglers return to what worked. A lane that has died twice, often with Flash still down, is his easiest gold on the map.
A counter gank there can flip the whole lane. Trading across the map is safer if your laner is too far behind to fight even with you.
Tell that laner to stop pushing either way. Under his own tower, the only way to keep camping him is a dive.
check: Is your laner there strong enough to fight with you, and does he have Flash? I can't see cooldowns.
breaks: If that lane is too far behind to win even three on two, stop feeding it attention. Mirror him on the other side instead.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: dragon spawns or respawns in under a minute
asks: where's he gonna be for dragon
is he coming to drake
dragon's up where's their jungler
he's heading bot right
say: With dragon close he's likely drifting bot. Get there first with your lanes, or let him have it and take top side camps and plates.
more: Objectives pull junglers on a schedule you can read off the clock. Dragon comes back five minutes after it dies.
Arriving first with a pushed wave means he has to walk into you. Arriving late and alone is the worst of both.
If your bot side can't move, a clean trade on the top half is worth more than a lost fight.
check: Do your mid and bot have their waves pushed, and is top side worth trading for right now?
breaks: If their jungler is dead or just showed top, don't trade at all. Take the dragon.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: game time between 7:00 and 8:00
asks: where's he going before grubs
is he coming top for grubs
grubs are soon where's their jungler
what's he doing at eight minutes
say: Grubs open at 8:00, so expect him top side. Meet him there with top and mid, or take dragon and bot plates while he does them.
more: Grubs are a single window and they don't come back. A jungler who wants them has to be top at eight.
That tells your bot lane they are safe for that minute, and tells you a cross-map trade is open.
Which is worth more depends on your team. Grubs help push towers; a dragon is a step on the clock toward soul.
check: Can your top and mid get to the pit first, and is dragon alive?
breaks: If he showed bot just before eight, flip it: the grubs are free and your bot lane needs to back off.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: game time past 20:00 and their jungler has not shown for a while
asks: where's their jungler baron's up
is he at baron
we can't see him late game
he's missing do we check baron
say: Late and missing usually means the Baron side. Check the pit as a group, or push a side wave and make him show.
more: From 20:00 Baron is the reason for almost everything a jungler does. An unseen jungler late is on that side until proven otherwise.
Face-checking it alone is how games end. Go together or use a wave to force them to answer somewhere you can see.
A pushed side lane also pulls one of them away from the pit, which makes the real check safer.
check: Is Baron alive, and are all five of your team alive and together?
breaks: If your team is split or someone is dead, don't check. Clear the nearest wave and wait for the respawn.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: their jungler is Evelynn and she is below level 6
asks: how do I track Evelynn
where's Evelynn before six
can I invade Evelynn
is Evelynn dangerous yet
say: Before six Evelynn is visible like anyone else. Find her on her camps and fight her there, or use these minutes to push your lanes.
more: Demon Shade only gives her camouflage after level 6. Until then normal wards see her and she has to walk in like any jungler.
Every camp you take from her delays that level. A late six for her means more safe minutes for your whole team.
After six the plan changes to control wards and keeping lanes healthy, so bank the lead now.
check: Which side did she start, and do your lanes on that side have push?
breaks: If your champion loses the early duel to her, skip the invade and spend the window ganking instead.
basis: kit:Evelynn

when: their jungler is Evelynn and she is level 6 or higher
asks: Evelynn's six now what
how do I see Evelynn coming
where's Evelynn
how do we stop Evelynn ganks
say: At six Evelynn is camouflaged out of combat, so normal wards miss her. Put control wards in river, or keep healthy with the wave back.
more: Demon Shade camouflages her once she is level 6. Allure only charms after a delay, so backing off the moment you see the mark on you often saves you.
She wants low, alone targets. A healthy lane with the wave on its own side is a bad gank for her.
Track her by the scoreboard instead of the map: her CS rising means she is farming, flat means she is waiting somewhere.
check: Do you have a control ward down, and is your lane healthy? I can't see wards.
breaks: If she's ahead on items, wards alone won't save a lone carry. Group for the next objective and stop taking side waves alone.
basis: kit:Evelynn

when: their jungler is Shaco
asks: where's Shaco
is Shaco gonna gank early
how do I track Shaco
Shaco level two gank
say: Shaco can go invisible and often ganks very early. Hold your wave back until he shows, or ward your own buff to catch an invade.
more: Deceive makes him invisible and blinks him a short way, so he arrives from angles a normal jungler can't use.
His Jack In The Box traps are hidden too, so walking into his jungle or a brush he has visited is riskier than it looks.
Once he shows in a kill event you know his side. Until then, the lane with no ward should not be the one pushing.
check: Did either of their side lanes arrive late? And is your buff still there?
breaks: If he's shown on the far side, you get a normal window. Push then, and step back again when he disappears.
basis: kit:Shaco

when: their jungler is Nocturne and he is level 6 or higher
asks: Nocturne's six where's he going
who's Nocturne gonna ult
how do I play around Nocturne ult
Nocturne is missing
say: At six Nocturne can dim your map and launch onto a laner. Keep the weakest lane near tower, or shadow it and turn on him.
more: Paranoia cuts your sight and your shared vision, then lets him launch at a champion, so he doesn't need to walk the usual gank path.
He tends to pick the target that dies fastest: low health, pushed up, no Flash. You can guess it as well as he can.
Standing near that lane turns his ultimate into a fight he didn't plan for.
check: Which of your lanes is low or pushed up without Flash? I can't see their health or cooldowns.
breaks: If you're too far behind to win the turn, don't shadow. Take a cross-map objective the moment the screen goes dark.
basis: kit:Nocturne

when: their jungler is Rengar and he is level 6 or higher
asks: where's Rengar
Rengar's got ult now
how do I not get one shot by Rengar
who's Rengar hunting
say: Rengar's ultimate camouflages him and shows him the nearest of you. Stay two together, or keep a control ward down and hug tower while he's missing.
more: Thrill of the Hunt camouflages him and reveals the nearest enemy champion to him. He has usually chosen his target before you know he is there.
Before six, his basic attack becomes a leap while he's in brush, so lanes with long brush are where his ganks start.
A second person next to the target is usually enough to make him look elsewhere.
check: Who on your team is alone in a side lane right now, and do you have a control ward?
breaks: If he's far ahead, two together may not be enough. Give the side wave and stay with the team until he shows.
basis: kit:Rengar

when: their jungler is Warwick
asks: where's Warwick
is Warwick coming for me
I'm low and they have Warwick
how do I track Warwick
say: Warwick senses anyone under half health and speeds toward them. Recall when you're low, or stay under tower with your jungler close.
more: Blood Hunt gives him move speed toward enemies below half health, and more when they are very low. A low laner is a beacon for him.
That makes him easier to predict: he often goes to whichever lane just lost a trade.
As a jungler you can use that. Wait near your low laner and you know where the fight will be.
check: How low are your laners? I only see your own health.
breaks: If your lane is healthy he has no special pull toward it. Then treat him like any other jungler and track his camps.
basis: kit:Warwick

when: their jungler is Fiddlesticks and he is level 6 or higher
asks: where's Fiddle
Fiddlesticks is six
how do we stop Fiddle ult
is Fiddle in that bush
say: Fiddlesticks wants to ult from somewhere unseen. Ward the brush and walls beside your fight, or fight in the open away from them.
more: Terrify fears when his spells hit you while he's unseen, so Crowstorm is far worse when it starts from somewhere you have no vision.
His trinket is scarecrow effigies, so a Fiddlesticks you can see standing still may not be him.
Before six he mostly wants camps. That is the time to push lanes and put pressure on his jungle.
check: Is the brush next to the objective warded? I can't see vision.
breaks: If you have no wards left, don't start the objective. Back off one screen and make him walk to you.
basis: kit:Fiddlesticks

when: their jungler is Zac
asks: where's Zac gonna come from
how do I ward against Zac
Zac keeps jumping over the wall
is Zac near
say: Zac launches in from well past normal ward spots. Ward deeper than usual, or keep your wave on your side so the jump lands short.
more: Elastic Slingshot throws him a long way, so he can start a gank from inside his own jungle or behind a wall.
A river ward often sees nothing because he never walks through river. A ward on the approach inside his jungle does.
The slingshot takes time to charge. A lane that is already backing off when he appears usually gets away.
check: How far up is your wave, and is there a ward past the river?
breaks: If you can't get a deep ward down safely, don't go for it alone. Just play the wave near your tower until he shows.
basis: kit:Zac

when: their jungler is Rek'Sai
asks: where's Rek'Sai
how does Rek'Sai get around so fast
do I break Rek'Sai's tunnels
how do I track Rek'Sai
say: Rek'Sai's tunnels last and let her cross walls again later. Stand on a tunnel end to break it, or ward where her tunnels come out.
more: While burrowed she leaves reusable tunnels. Each one is a shortcut she can take on her next visit to that area.
Breaking a tunnel near your lane makes her next gank slower and more visible.
Burrowing gives her move speed, but she can't basic attack until she comes up. The moment she surfaces is when the gank really starts.
check: Have you seen a tunnel entrance near your lane or jungle?
breaks: If breaking it means walking into fog alone, leave it. A ward watching the exit does the same job safely.
basis: kit:Rek'Sai

when: their jungler is Karthus and he is level 6 or higher
asks: Karthus has ult what do I do
where's Karthus
Karthus is just farming
how do we play against Karthus jungle
say: Karthus's ultimate hits all of you wherever he is. Once he's six, recall after a losing trade, or stay only if you'd survive it.
more: Requiem hits every enemy champion after a three second channel, wherever he is. He doesn't need to be near your lane to get the kill.
That means his position matters less than your health. Low laners should leave, not stay for one more wave.
Death Defied lets him keep casting after he dies, so killing him in a fight doesn't make a low teammate safe yet.
He still needs farm to make it hurt. Taking his camps when he shows elsewhere is the long-term answer.
check: Who on your team is low right now? I only see your own health.
breaks: If he's dead and his spirit form is over, or Requiem just went off, that's your window to take the low-health trade you'd normally avoid.
basis: kit:Karthus

when: their jungler is Kha'Zix
asks: where's Kha'Zix
who's Kha'Zix going for
how do I fight Kha'Zix
Kha'Zix keeps catching me
say: Kha'Zix hits hardest on anyone alone. Cross river only with a laner close, or farm the side away from where he last showed.
more: Unseen Threat marks enemies isolated from their allies, and Taste Their Fear does more damage to them. A lone jungler between camps is the target he wants.
At six Void Assault makes him invisible and triggers Unseen Threat again, so being alone gets even more expensive.
You track him by denying the pick: if nobody is alone, he has to show up to a real fight.
check: Is an ally close to you right now, and which side did he last show on?
breaks: If you're well ahead of him you can take the duel anyway. Otherwise keep a laner within reach when you cross river.
basis: kit:Kha'Zix

when: their jungler got a kill or assist on your top laner in the last 30 seconds
asks: he's top can I take his bot camps
he showed top do I invade
should I counter jungle now
he's top what do I take
say: He just showed top, so his bot side is empty. Take a camp or two there, or gank bot while he can't answer.
more: Kill events are the best tracking the game gives you. He was in that lane a few seconds ago, so he can't be on his bot camps yet.
Camps set him back quietly and keep you on pace. A gank is the higher payoff if their bot lane is pushed up.
Whichever you choose, do it right away. This window is as long as his walk.
check: Is their bot lane pushed toward your tower, and is their mid in lane?
breaks: If their mid is missing, skip his jungle. Take your own bot camps and look at the lane from the safe side.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: their jungler got a kill or assist on your bot lane or took dragon in the last 30 seconds
asks: he's bot do I take his top side
he showed bot what do I steal
can I invade top now
he's at dragon what do I do
say: He's bot, so his top side is open. Clear his top camps for the farm lead, or use the time on grubs or a top gank.
more: You can't undo what he just got. You can make sure it cost him half his jungle.
His top camps put you ahead in levels. An objective or a kill top puts your team ahead in gold.
Standing still because bot went badly is the only wrong answer.
check: Is your top laner able to move with you, and are grubs or herald alive?
breaks: If you were already bot side and your lane is still alive, help there instead. If their top laner has the wave pushed toward you, take only the camp nearest river.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: he died can I take his jungle
their jungler's dead what do I take
should I invade now he's dead
he's dead do I steal his camps
say: He's dead, so take his camps on the side you're already on. Or grab the crab and gank that lane before he walks back.
more: An early death costs a jungler twice: the time dead, and whatever you remove while he's gone.
Each small camp you take is one he waits about 2:15 for. That can leave him a level down for the next big fight.
A gank instead spreads the lead to a laner. Pick based on which lane can actually kill.
check: How long is his timer, and are their laners on that side still in lane?
breaks: If their laners there are healthy and their wave is pushed to you, they can collapse on you. Take only the camp nearest river and leave.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: you are at least one level above their jungler
asks: I'm ahead do I invade
should I go into his jungle
I'm a level up can I counter jungle
do I take his camps
say: With a level lead you can take his camps if your nearest lane has push. Otherwise ward his jungle and farm yours.
more: The duel is not what decides an invade. It ends when the nearest lane arrives, so the wave in that lane decides it.
One stolen camp per trip keeps him behind without risking the lead. Staying for three is how leads get thrown.
A ward left in his jungle keeps paying after you leave. It tells your lanes where he is for the next couple of minutes.
check: Does your lane beside his jungle have its wave pushed in?
breaks: If that lane is pushed toward your tower instead, their laner gets there first. Skip it and take the other side.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: their jungler is at least one level above you
asks: I'm behind can I still counter jungle
should I invade when I'm behind
he's ahead do I steal camps
how do I catch up
say: Don't walk into him while behind. Take his opposite side only when he shows on the map, or just clear your camps as they respawn.
more: Meeting a stronger jungler in his own jungle turns a small deficit into a death.
What you can do is trade. When he appears in a kill or at an objective, the half of his jungle farthest away is safe for that moment.
Small camps come back about 2:15 after dying. Hitting every respawn on your side is the reliable way back into the game.
check: Where did he last show? Only go in if you know he's on the other side.
breaks: If he hasn't shown in a while, don't go at all. Farm your side nearest your strongest lane.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler is at or above your level and one of your side lanes is behind its opponent in CS
asks: he keeps invading me
he's taking my camps what do I do
I can't fight him in my jungle
do I defend my camps
say: Don't defend the side beside your losing lane. Give it and take his opposite side at the same time, or farm next to your winning lane.
more: He picks the half of your jungle where his laner can help and yours can't. Fighting him there is fighting two.
Swapping sides keeps your farm even. You lose camps, he loses the same ones on the far side.
It also pulls the game toward your stronger lane, which is where you want the next fights anyway.
check: Is he really winning the duel against you? And which of your lanes is under tower, and which has push?
breaks: If he's on your side and you still have a healthy lane with push right there, call them in and fight. Three beats two.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

asks: how long do I stay in his jungle
should I keep taking his camps
do I take one more camp
is it worth staying in there
say: Take one camp and get out. Stay for a second only if you know where he is, or leave a ward and return to your own.
more: Every second in his jungle is a second your own camps sit there. He knows where you are and has the far side to himself.
One camp and a ward is a clean profit. Three camps often ends with their mid and jungler finding you.
Check the scoreboard as you leave. If his CS climbed while you were in there, he was farming somewhere else, possibly your side.
check: Do you actually know where he is right now?
breaks: If he's dead or just showed across the map, staying for more is fine. Without that, one and out.
basis: pro:Time in their jungle is time given away

asks: when do his camps come back
how do I time stealing his camps
when should I go back to his jungle
can I steal his buff
say: Small camps return about 2:15 after dying, buffs after five minutes. Arrive just before the spawn to steal it, or ward it and catch him there.
more: A camp you took from him has a timer you know and he might not. That is a free second steal.
Buffs are the bigger prize and the bigger risk. He will come for it, often with a laner.
A ward on the camp is the low-risk version. You don't get the gold, but you know exactly where he'll be.
check: What time did that camp or buff die? I can't see camps, so you need the clock.
breaks: If their lane beside it has push when the timer comes up, don't go. Use the timer to gank the opposite side instead.
basis: rule

when: their jungler has two or more kills or assists on one side of the map and low CS for the time
asks: he's always bot are his top camps up
he lives bot side
he's not farming top can I take it
he's ignoring half his jungle
say: He's been living on one side, so his far camps are likely sitting there. Go clear them, or mirror him and counter gank his favorite lane.
more: Low CS with kills on one side means the other half of his jungle is being ignored.
Clearing it widens the farm gap he's already paying for. The longer he camps a lane, the more his own jungle becomes yours.
Counter ganking is the bolder play. It works if your laner there can still fight.
check: Which side has he been showing on, and is your lane there still able to fight?
breaks: If his laner on the far side has push, they can still catch you. Take the camps closest to river first.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: their jungler is a farm-scaling champion and you are even or ahead in level
asks: how do I shut down a farming jungler
he just wants to farm how do I punish
how do I stop him scaling
should I invade a farm jungler
say: A farming jungler hates losing camps most. Take one of his each clear with a lane ready, or gank more often while he farms.
more: His plan is to arrive at the mid game with more items than you. Every camp you remove pushes that date back.
The other answer is to use the time he gives you. If he never leaves his jungle, your ganks are uncontested.
Doing neither and matching him camp for camp is playing his game.
check: Do you win the duel if he catches you in there? I can't judge that for you.
breaks: If your champion scales better than his, don't bother. Farm alongside him and win later.
basis: written

when: their jungler is Bel'Veth
asks: how do I slow down Bel'Veth
should I invade Bel'Veth
Bel'Veth is scaling
how do I stop Bel'Veth
say: Bel'Veth grows off large monsters and takedowns. Take her big camps when she shows elsewhere, or keep fights clean so she gets no kills.
more: Death in Lavender gives her permanent attack speed from large monsters and from champion takedowns. Farm and kills are both progress for her.
So a messy early skirmish that trades one for one still feeds her. Clean objective trades are better than brawls.
Taking her camps is slow but it works on the thing she cares about most.
check: Where did she last show, and does your lane beside her jungle have push?
breaks: If you're the stronger duelist right now, fight her on her camps. Use it before she outgrows you.
basis: kit:Bel'Veth

when: their jungler is Ivern
asks: how do I counter jungle Ivern
Ivern is stealing my camps
where's Ivern
Ivern's in my jungle again
say: Ivern frees camps instead of fighting them, so he invades cheaply. Ward your buffs and meet him there, or take his camps while he's in yours.
more: He can't attack normal camps or be hit by them. He plants a grove that grows and then frees the monsters, so he loses no health clearing.
That means he shows up in your jungle healthy and early. It also means he has little to fight you with if you find him alone.
A ward on your buff tells you which it is: stealing, or passing through to a lane.
check: Is your buff warded, and can you beat him one on one if you find him?
breaks: If he arrives with a laner, back off. Trade for his camps on the other side.
basis: kit:Ivern

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: he's dead mid game what do I take
their jungler died do I invade or objective
what's free now
he's dead what's the best thing to take
say: With him dead, take the objective if one's up, or take his buffs and ward his jungle for the next fight if nothing is.
more: Without Smite on their side, an epic monster is close to free. That beats any number of camps.
If nothing is alive, his jungle is the next best use. Camps you take and wards you leave decide who walks into the next objective blind.
Push the nearest wave first if you can. It stops their laners from coming to stop you.
check: Is dragon, herald or Baron alive right now, and how long is his timer?
breaks: If three or more of them are alive and nearby and your team isn't with you, take the wave and one camp only.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

asks: my jungler's invading do I go
should I help my jungler in their jungle
do I follow the invade
jungler's pinging their buff
say: If your wave is pushed, go with him; arriving first wins it. If you're shoved in, ping him out instead.
more: An invade is decided by which lane next to it moves first. Your jungler is betting on you.
Pushing the wave before you leave means you lose nothing and their laner has to choose between farm and helping.
If you can't move, tell him early. A jungler who knows he's alone can leave before it turns.
check: Is your jungler actually stronger than theirs right now? Where is your wave, and has their laner already left?
breaks: If their laner left first and you can't follow, shove the wave and take plates. Make them pay for it somewhere.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: game time past 20:00 and their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: their jungler's dead late what do we do
he's dead do we baron
no smite on their team right now
jungler's down what do we take
say: Their Smite is gone, so Baron or the dragon is the call if it's up. If it isn't, push a wave and clear their jungle camps.
more: Late on, an epic monster usually comes down to the Smite. With their jungler dead, that contest is gone.
Death timers are long now, so there's usually time to finish. Don't spend it chasing a second kill.
If nothing is alive, taking their camps and vision sets up the next spawn.
check: Is Baron or dragon alive, how long is his timer, and how many of you are up?
breaks: If you're too low on health or numbers to finish before he's back, drop it. Reset and set up vision instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

asks: should I counter gank
where do I sit for a counter gank
which lane is he gonna gank
how do I shadow their jungler
say: Shadow the lane he most wants: yours that's pushed up without Flash. Farm the camps beside it and wait, or gank the opposite side.
more: A counter gank beats a gank because you arrive second with everything up. The trick is guessing the lane.
He goes where it's easy. Pushed wave, no Flash, already lost a trade.
Waiting has a price. If nothing happens within a camp or two, go back to farming so you don't fall behind.
check: Which of your lanes is pushed up or missing Flash? I can't see wave position.
breaks: If he shows on the other side while you wait, stop waiting. Gank the lane you're next to right away.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

when: their jungler got a kill or assist in the last 30 seconds
asks: he just ganked where do I go
he showed do I gank now
which lane do I gank now
he's on the other side what now
say: He just showed, so gank the lane farthest from that kill for a real numbers edge. Or take an objective on your side if it's up.
more: For a short while you know where he is and he doesn't know where you are. That is the best time to commit.
A gank needs a lane that can follow up. An objective only needs him to be far away.
If neither is there, take his camps on your side. Just don't let the window pass.
check: Which lane is farthest from where he showed, and is that enemy pushed up?
breaks: If you were already next to the lane he ganked and your laner is alive, go there. A counter gank beats a cross-map trade.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: he's dead should I gank or dive
their jungler's dead which lane
can we dive now
he's dead where do I go
say: With him dead, a dive is as safe as it gets. Dive the lane with a big wave, or take the objective if one's up.
more: The usual risk in a dive is their jungler arriving behind you. That risk is on a timer right now.
You still need minions under the tower and their escape tool down or baited. Numbers alone don't make it safe.
If no lane has a wave ready, the objective is the cleaner pick.
check: Which lane has a wave about to hit their tower, and how long is his timer?
breaks: If no wave is crashing, skip the dive. Take the objective, or his camps if nothing's up.
basis: pro:A dive runs on minions and one defensive button

when: an ally died to their jungler in the last 30 seconds
asks: my laner just died do I go there
should I go help after he ganked
he killed my top do I go
do I trade or go avenge
say: That fight is over, so don't walk into it late. Take something on the far side now, or cover the wave if he's already gone.
more: Arriving after the kill means meeting a jungler and a laner with the wave on their side. That usually makes it two deaths.
The trade has to be real: a kill, plates, a dragon or his camps. Hovering halfway gets you nothing.
Covering the wave is fine if you can see he has left. It saves your laner a lot of farm.
check: Did their jungler stay in that lane, and what is actually takeable on the far side?
breaks: If he's low on health from the fight and their laner is too, going there with a healthy teammate can clean both up.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

asks: should I gank that lane again
my gank failed do I go back
do I keep trying top
he keeps escaping
say: If they burned Flash, go back before it's up. If nothing changed, pick a lane that can set it up, or just farm.
more: A gank that failed for a reason will fail again for the same reason. Their jungler also knows where you just were.
If you burned a Flash, that's a real change. Returning before it's back is one of the best ganks there is.
If nothing changed, the time is better spent on camps or another lane.
check: Did your last gank there fail, and did they use Flash or another escape? I can't see ganks or cooldowns. Is the wave in a better spot now?
breaks: If their jungler started shadowing that lane after your first try, the repeat is a trap. Go opposite.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: before 3:00
asks: do I gank early or full clear
should I gank at three
is an early gank worth it
their lane is fighting do I go
say: If a lane is fighting hard with no ward, a short clear into it can pay. Otherwise full clear and meet him at the crab.
more: Lanes that brawl at level one or two are often low and missing summoner spells by the time you arrive.
The price is camps. If the gank gets nothing, their jungler finishes a full clear a level ahead of you.
So it has to be a lane where the fight is already happening, not one you hope will start.
check: Is that lane actually trading hard, and did they put a ward down?
breaks: If their jungler started on that same side, you may be walking into him. Full clear instead.
basis: pro:A lane that fights early without a ward invites a short clear

when: their jungler is level 6 and you are level 5
asks: where do I gank when he's six
he has ult where can I gank safely
which lane is safe to gank
do I still gank
say: Gank only where he can't answer: far from where he last showed. Or hold off and farm to six first.
more: A gank that he counters while a level up is a lost two on two and usually a double kill for them.
Distance is your protection. If he just showed bot, top is safe for one play.
A quick six evens it out, and then you can gank wherever the lane is good.
check: Where did he last show, and how long ago?
breaks: If he hasn't shown recently, don't gank at all. Take camps until you're six.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

when: their jungler's item list just gained an item (not a used potion or ward)
asks: he just recalled do I gank
he's in base which lane
he backed can I go now
is this a gank window
say: He's in base buying, so a quick gank now can't be countered by him. Take the lane that's ready, or start the objective if it's close.
more: A jungler at the fountain can't counter gank. You have roughly his walk back to river, so the lane has to be ready now.
Keep it short. He comes back with an item, and a fight that drags on meets a stronger jungler.
If no lane is ready, use it for vision in his jungle instead.
check: Which lane is ready right now, without you waiting for the wave?
breaks: If the gank needs a long setup, he'll be back before it lands. Take camps and ward instead.
basis: pro:Their jungler or carry in base is your window

when: both junglers have a kill or assist on the same lane in the last minute
asks: we're both on the same side now what
he's here too do I stay
we both ganked bot what next
do I stay bot or leave
say: You're both on one side, so the other half is empty. Stay if your lane wins the fight, or leave first and take the far side.
more: When both junglers commit to one lane, whoever leaves first gets the rest of the map for free.
Staying is right if your side has the wave and the health. Then he has to leave or lose more.
If it's even, breaking the stalemate by going top is usually worth more than waiting for someone to blink.
check: Who has the wave and the health in that lane now?
breaks: If your lane is low and can't hold without you, stay until they recall. Leaving gets them dived.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: their jungler got a kill or assist on another lane in the last 30 seconds
asks: can I ask for a gank now
should I set up for my jungler
he's on the other side do I push or freeze
how do I use this
say: He showed elsewhere, so pick: hold the wave on your side to set up a gank, or push it in for plates and a recall.
more: With their jungler accounted for, your own jungler's gank is much harder to counter. A wave near your tower gives it room to work.
Pushing is the solo option. It needs nobody's help and gets you gold and a safe recall.
Tell your jungler which you're doing. The worst version is a pushed wave and a jungler arriving to nothing.
check: Where is your own jungler? If he's across the map, push.
breaks: If your jungler is dead or far away, don't freeze for a gank that isn't coming. Shove and recall.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: their jungler got a kill, assist or objective on one side in the last 30 seconds
asks: he showed on a side lane mid game
he's bot what do we do as a team
their jungler's top where do we go
he showed do we force something
say: He's shown on one side, so force on the other. Start the objective there, or group and take a tower before he crosses.
more: In the mid game a jungler on the wrong side means his team is four against five wherever you go.
An objective is the best use if one is up. A tower is next: outer towers are also their vision.
It only works if you move together and right away.
check: What's up on the far side, and is your team close enough to move as a group?
breaks: If your team is scattered, don't start anything. Push the nearest wave and reset vision.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: their jungler is an assassin and has more kills than you
asks: he's fed where do I gank
their assassin jungler is ahead
how do I gank when he one shots me
do I still go to lanes
say: Don't move alone where he could be. Gank with a laner beside you, or stay near your carry and turn when he jumps in.
more: A fed assassin wins by catching one person. Your ganks have to stop offering him that.
Counter ganking is your best tool now. He has to come to your carries, so you know where the fight will be.
Outer towers falling makes it worse, because your vision shrinks. Hold the ones you have.
check: Who is he most likely to go for, and are you close enough to them?
breaks: If he shows across the map, drop the bodyguard job for that moment and take the free play.

when: an enemy laner is dead with a respawn timer
asks: their laner's dead do I go there
their top is dead what do I do
lane's empty should I come
can I take plates
say: That lane is empty, so their jungler may come to catch the wave. Help shove it and take plates, or use that to gank elsewhere.
more: A dead laner leaves farm on the table. Junglers often show up to collect it, which tells you where he is.
Pushing with your laner turns the kill into plates. If he does come, you have the numbers.
If your laner can push alone, a gank elsewhere while he's busy catching the wave is even better.
check: Can your laner shove that wave alone, or do they need you?
breaks: If your laner is too low to stay, don't hold the lane alone for long. Take the nearest camp of his and go.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: their jungler just reached level 4 and game time is before 4:30
asks: their jungler's level four
is his first clear done
he just hit four where is he
is he ganking now
say: He's level 4, so his first clear is likely done and he's free to gank. Pull the wave back, or ward river and keep trading.
more: One full clear is about level 4. When that number appears on the scoreboard, he has probably run out of camps and is looking at a crab or a lane.
Before that level shows, a gank costs him camps. After it, ganking is free for him until his camps come back.
If he then shows on the far side, you get the push back and can crash the wave before recalling.
check: Which side did he start on, and is your river warded? I can't see wards or where he is.
breaks: If he got to 4 from an early kill, he may still have camps left to take. Go by where that kill happened instead.
basis: rule

when: their jungler is alive, his CS has not risen for about a minute, and he has no kill, assist or objective event in that time
asks: his cs hasn't moved
where is he he's not farming
is he sitting in a bush
their jungler stopped farming
is he camping someone
say: His farm has stalled and he hasn't shown, so he may be waiting nearby. Back off until he appears, or ward and farm near tower.
more: A jungler's CS only goes up when he takes camps. Flat farm with no kills means he is walking, waiting in a brush, or in base.
You can't tell which lane from the numbers, so every pushed-up lane should treat it as theirs for now.
The moment his CS ticks up or he appears in a kill, the warning is over and you can step forward again.
check: Which of your lanes is pushed up right now, and did his items just change? A new item means he was only recalling.
breaks: If all his camps were just cleared or stolen he has nothing to farm either. Then he is likelier at an objective; check what spawns next.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: their jungler's CS rose in the last 15 seconds and he has not shown in a kill event
asks: is he farming right now
his cs just went up
is he on a camp
can I trade right now
is it safe for a second
say: His farm just went up, so he's on a camp, not in your brush. Trade or push for a few seconds, or ward river now.
more: His CS climbing is a live signal that he is hitting monsters somewhere. It is the closest thing to a sighting the scoreboard gives you.
It doesn't say which camp. The window is short if the camp he took is the one beside your lane.
Use it for something quick: a trade, a ward, or a shove you were holding back on.
check: Do you know which side of the map he is on? I see his farm go up, not where the camp was.
breaks: If he last showed on your side, that camp may be right next to you. Take the ward, not the trade.
basis: written

when: their jungler's item list just gained an item (not a used potion or ward)
asks: their jungler just backed right
he bought something am I safe
he's in base can I push
their jungler has a new item
say: He just bought, so he's at base for a moment. Shove the wave or take a trade now, or recall too and match the item.
more: Items can only be bought at the fountain, so a new one tells you he is as far from your lane as he can be.
